about.author: Zyphullen

automatic_checks.what: Structural checks run by a script on every build (src/audit.py, report in AUDIT-v0.7.md): every card has a colour and at least one source, links point at cards that exist, share links are exact, the data hash is the same in every file, counts match, and every source URL was fetched to see that it answers.
automatic_checks.not: They do not read the science. Passing them does not mean a claim is right, only that it is labelled, sourced and linked.

science_review.what: A science review means a person with the right expertise reads each claim against its sources and decides whether it is right, up to date and fairly coloured.
science_review.how_to_help: Every card has a Suggest a fix button (e-mail). Please check claims against the listed sources and say what looks wrong.

about.certainty_rule: green = established (known science, or a defined / proved result in Maths); orange = leading idea / partial progress; red = unknown / open problem. A link takes the colour of its less-certain end.

suggest_a_fix.subject: Echo Atlas fix: <Card name> (<card id>)
suggest_a_fix.note: Every card has a Suggest a fix button that opens a prefilled e-mail (section, card, card id, version, page link). Card ids: fntu/<id>, maths/<id>, history/<id>-<n>, cell/<id>, body/<id>, planet/<id>, element/<symbol>, <section>/link/<from>><to>.

about.what_this_file_holds: A dated timeline of the universe from the Big Bang to today: the first second, the first nuclei and light, cosmic dawn, galaxies and the Sun, Earth and life. The time scale changes between eras. On the site it is also the History view of From Nothing to Us (Explore → From Nothing to Us → History).
about.already_in_this_file: This file already holds everything for this section: the facts (summary, details), the colours (certainty), the sources (title, url, type, year, link check) and the connections between ideas, including links to cards in other sections (rel / related / section_links, each with the other section name and id). Load another section file only when you want the full card on the other end of a link.
about.how_to_use: Every item has id, title, certainty, summary, details and sources (title, url, type). Full source details (year, link check) are in sources_used. A link's reason_sources are the sources on its two cards. Fact-check against the sources; flag anything that looks wrong or out of date.

big_bang_to_today.note: Selected dated events from the Big Bang to today. The time scale changes between eras (logarithmic early on) so each era is readable; it is not a linear time line.

events.title: Before the Big Bang?
summary: Whether there was a "before", and what it was, is unknown. Known physics cannot reach back this far.

sources.title: Carlip 2001: quantum gravity, a progress report (Rep. Prog. Phys.)
Wikipedia: Chronology of the universe

events.title: Planck epoch
summary: Gravity and quantum effects are both strong. No tested theory describes this first instant.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Planck units
Wikipedia: Chronology of the universe
Carlip 2001: quantum gravity, a progress report (Rep. Prog. Phys.)

events.title: Cosmic inflation
summary: A leading idea: a split-second burst of expansion made the universe smooth and flat and seeded its ripples. The cosmic microwave background fits it; its gravitational-wave signal has not been found.

sources.title: Planck 2018 results X: constraints on inflation
Guth 1981: the inflationary universe (Phys. Rev. D)
BICEP/Keck + others: r < 0.034
Wikipedia: Cosmic inflation

events.title: End of the electroweak epoch
summary: The Higgs field takes its value: the weak and electromagnetic forces separate, and the W and Z bosons, quarks and electrons gain mass. The LHC recreates these energies.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Electroweak epoch
PDG 2024 review: Big-Bang cosmology (hot early universe, neutrino decoupling)
OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 11.7 Evolution of the Early Universe

events.title: Quarks bind into hadrons
summary: The quark–gluon plasma cools below about 156 MeV (~1.8 trillion kelvin) and quarks become bound into protons and neutrons.

sources.title: HotQCD 2019: quarks and gluons free up near 156 MeV (~1.8×10¹² K) (Phys. Lett. B)
STAR 2005: evidence for quark–gluon plasma at RHIC (Nucl. Phys. A)
Wikipedia: Quark epoch

events.title: Neutrinos decouple
summary: Neutrinos stop interacting and fly free. This cosmic neutrino background has not been seen directly, but its effect shows in the early-universe light and the first nuclei.

sources.title: PDG 2024 review: Big-Bang cosmology (hot early universe, neutrino decoupling)
Wikipedia: Cosmic neutrino background

events.title: Big Bang nucleosynthesis
summary: The first nuclei form: about 75% hydrogen and 25% helium by mass, with traces of deuterium and lithium.

sources.title: PDG review: Big-Bang nucleosynthesis
Wikipedia: Big Bang nucleosynthesis
OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 11.7 Evolution of the Early Universe

events.title: Recombination
summary: The universe cools to about 3,000 K, electrons join nuclei to make the first atoms, and light travels freely: the cosmic microwave background.

sources.title: Planck 2018 results VI: cosmological parameters
Penzias & Wilson 1965: A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s. (ApJ)
Wikipedia: Recombination (cosmology)

events.title: First stars
summary: The first stars, made only of hydrogen and helium, probably formed within the first few hundred million years. None has been seen directly yet; a 2026 candidate (Hebe) is being studied.

sources.title: Bromm 2013: formation of the first stars (Rep. Prog. Phys.)
"Hebe": a helium emitter at z = 10.6, first-star candidate (2026)
Second team on Hebe (2026)

events.title: Earliest galaxies seen
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has seen a galaxy (MoM-z14) as it was about 280 million years after the Big Bang.

sources.title: Naidu et al. 2025: MoM-z14, a galaxy 280 million years after the Big Bang

events.title: End of reionization
summary: Light from the first stars and galaxies ionised the gas between galaxies again; quasar spectra show this was complete by about a billion years after the Big Bang.

sources.title: Fan et al. 2006: Observational Constraints on Cosmic Reionization (Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.)
Wikipedia: Reionization

events.title: Expansion starts to speed up
summary: Dark energy begins to dominate and the expansion of the universe speeds up. Found from distant supernovae in 1998; what dark energy is remains unknown.

sources.title: Riess et al. 1998: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe and a Cosmological Constant (The Astronomical Journal)
Perlmutter et al. 1999: Measurements of Ω and Λ from 42 High‐Redshift Supernovae (ApJ)
Riess et al. 2004: Type Ia Supernova Discoveries at z > 1 from the Hubble Space Telescope: Evidence for Past Deceleration and Constraints on Dark Energy Evolution (ApJ)
Wikipedia: Accelerating expansion of the universe

events.title: Sun and Solar System form
summary: The oldest solids in meteorites date the birth of the Solar System to 4,567 million years ago.

sources.title: Connelly et al. 2012 (Science): CAIs are 4567.30 ± 0.16 million years old
Wikipedia: Formation and evolution of the Solar System

events.title: Earth and Moon form
summary: Earth forms; the leading idea is that the Moon formed after a Mars-sized body (Theia) hit the young Earth.

sources.title: Canup & Asphaug 2001: the Moon from a giant impact (Nature)
Max Planck (MPS): Theia and Earth were neighbours
Science 2025: iron isotopes of Earth and Moon (Theia)

events.title: Oldest evidence of water
summary: Tiny zircon crystals show liquid water on Earth’s surface about 4.4 billion years ago.

sources.title: Wilde et al. 2001: water on Earth 4.4 billion years ago (Nature)

events.title: Last universal common ancestor
summary: All life shares one ancestor; a 2024 study estimates it lived about 4.2 billion years ago.

sources.title: Moody et al. 2024: LUCA ~4.2 billion years ago (Nat. Ecol. Evol.)

events.title: Oldest widely accepted fossils
summary: Stromatolites in the Dresser Formation of Western Australia record microbial life about 3.48 billion years ago.

sources.title: Djokic et al. 2017: ~3.5-billion-year-old life signs, Dresser Formation (Nat. Commun.)

events.title: Great Oxidation Event
summary: Oxygen made by photosynthesis builds up in the air for the first time.

sources.title: Lyons, Reinhard & Planavsky 2014: the rise of oxygen (Nature)

events.title: Cambrian explosion
summary: Most major animal groups appear in the fossil record within a few tens of millions of years.

sources.title: International Commission on Stratigraphy: chart 2024/12 (Cambrian base 538.8 Ma)

events.title: Earliest primates
summary: The oldest primate fossils date to just after the extinction of the non-bird dinosaurs.

sources.title: Wilson Mantilla et al. 2021 (R. Soc. Open Sci.): oldest primate fossils, ~65.9 million yr

events.title: Homo sapiens
summary: The oldest known fossils of our species, from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco.

sources.title: Hublin et al. 2017: Homo sapiens ~300,000 years old (Nature)

events.title: Today
events.when: 13.8 billion years after the Big Bang
summary: The universe is 13.787 ± 0.020 billion years old (Planck). Still open: the Hubble tension, where two ways of measuring today's expansion rate disagree.

sources.title: Planck 2018 results VI: cosmological parameters
H0 Distance Network 2025: H0 = 73.50 ± 0.81, 7.1σ from early-universe value
